q1.prompt: You build a long string by appending characters one by one in a loop. Which approach stays cheap?

choices.label: Grow a mutable buffer (or list of chunks), then join once
Repeated string + in an immutable language

wrong_concat.prompt: Each + can copy the whole prefix.
wrong_concat.explanation: In languages that copy on concatenation, repeated + inside a loop is O(n²). Collect chunks and join once, or use a mutable buffer.

q2.prompt: Which claim hides the cost of immutable strings?

choices.label: When the runtime copies on each edit and n is large
Never — character writes are always O(1)

wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid repeated concatenation in a hot loop when the language copies on each +. Avoid treating a string edit as O(1) without stating whether the runtime mutates in place.

success.prompt: You chose buffers over repeated + and avoided free-edit claims when copies dominate.
